question: In 1866, who organised the East India Association in London to discuss the Indian question and to influence British public officials to promote Indian welfare?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** organized the East India Association in London in 1866.
 
• The association was established to discuss the Indian question and influence British public officials to promote Indian welfare.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji is often referred to as the "Grand Old Man of India" and was a prominent Indian political leader and social reformer.
 
• The East India Association played a significant role in advocating for Indian interests and raising awareness about the conditions in India under British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was also the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament, representing the Finsbury Central constituency from 1892 to 1895.
 
• He was a co-founder of the Indian National Congress and played a key role in the early years of India's independence movement.
 
• Naoroji's work and writings, including his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India," highlighted the economic exploitation of India by the British.
 
• He is also known for his theory of the "Drain of Wealth," which argued that India was being impoverished by the British economic policies.
